hyps.why: Raising an already large learning rate causes divergence and large accuracy drops on all datasets.
Lowering a very large learning rate restores stable training, giving big gains.
Increasing already strong L2 penalty over-regularizes and underfits.
Relaxing a strong L2 penalty reduces underfitting.
With a tiny learning rate and a fixed 243 epochs, models are undertrained and benefit from faster steps.
Lowering an already small learning rate worsens undertraining within the fixed epoch budget.
Deeper networks are more unstable at high learning rates, so adding depth hurts there.
Wider layers amplify update magnitude at high learning rates, increasing divergence.
Narrower layers are more stable under large learning rates.
Very small batches give noisy gradients, so moderately larger batches help.
